status: User accepted both exact integer-constant matcher diagnostics on 2026-10-07. Full RPM and native architecture qualification remain separate gates.
root_cause: The compiler does not preserve the relationship between the IsIntConstant preconditions and the output assignments in MatchSignedIntegralConstant. Both predicates accept exactly the same Word32/Word64 kinds; accepted calls initialize the output before returning true.
source_review: TryNarrowOpcodeSize calls MachineTypeForNarrowWordAnd at two sites, each guarding the comparison operand with IsIntConstant.
MachineTypeForNarrowWordAnd selects an AND operand with the same IsIntConstant guard and only enters the matching branch when that index is valid.

The unchanged matcher assigns signed_integral() and returns true for exactly Word32 and Word64. All rejected kinds leave the output untouched. Graph inputs are read from the same compiler graph during selection.
For nonnegative inputs, the selected width covers both constants; negative or out-of-range values retain the original full-width instruction.

coverage.matrix: All combinations of 22 signed/boundary values, Word32/Word64 on each constant and both AND input positions, repeated 100 times. Every declared constant kind tests predicate/matcher agreement and unchanged rejected output; no-constant AND and two-constant priority are covered.
coverage.native_modes: Release/debug, normally and under Valgrind; both memory runs have zero errors and all allocations freed.
coverage.compiler: The cmp_constant diagnostic reproduces in both builds; the smaller control does not reproduce and_constant.
coverage.javascript: 576 functions cover eight masks, twelve boundary constants and six comparison operators over fourteen signed inputs. Results match an independent BigInt reference; TurboFan optimization is requested and verified.

limits: The original constant-kind enum, signed conversion, predicate, matcher and narrowing body are verbatim. Typed graph/index and MachineType adapters do not emit machine code.
Native tests cover 64-bit matching; actual JavaScript masked comparisons exercise 32-bit bitwise semantics. No claim of actual generated-code coverage for all 64-bit native cases is made.
Only one of the two full-build warnings reproduces in the smaller control. The second is supported by the identical predicate/matcher contract and source call-path review.
No runtime patch, diagnostic suppression or compiler-flag change is proposed.
